answer: Gate admission on network-topology scarcity: each agent seat must answer from a distinct routable IP prefix under a separate autonomous system, proven by a signed BGP-path probe. The registry is a vault binding every prefix to one vertex in the trust graph; clones sharing an upstream collapse into a single vertex and forfeit their bond. Since a /24 block and an AS number are RIR-registered scarce resources, one operator cannot ripple 500 fake seats across 500 prefixes without 500 real, costly allocations, so each fake costs a genuine address registration, not a free copy.
